Varieties
Collard varieties include the Plant Vates,
Carolina Improved Heading (or Morris),
Georgia Southern, Blue Max, and Heavi
Crop.
Origin & botanical facts
Collards, one of the oldest members of
the cabbage family, are similar to the wild,
nonheading forms of cabbage that were
among the first foods eaten by prehistoric
people.  They are native to the eastern
Mediterranean region and Asia Minor
and were cultivated by the ancient Greeks
and Romans.  Collards were introduced
to Britain and France around 400 B.C. by
either the Romans or the Celts.  Although
